brief: GS forecasts hyperscaler capex of $1.2tn in 2027 and $1.4tn in 2028, above consensus but decelerating from roughly 98% growth in 2026 to 54% in 2027 and 12% in 2028; funding is shifting toward private credit and equity because capex now exceeds operating cash flow and investment-grade bond capacity is the binding constraint. To break even on average 2026-2027 capex, hyperscalers need about $300bn in annual AI revenue; incremental cloud revenue is already running near $70bn above the pre-AI trend in Q2 2026, backed by a $1.7tn backlog across AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT. For the application layer to also earn adequate margins on that compute spend, GS sizes required annual revenue as high as $1tn-plus at a 30% EBIT margin and 10-20% ROIC, comparable to $1.5tn in global software spending and a potential $1.8tn in AI-driven US productivity gains, not all of which will flow to infrastructure or application layers. On pricing, AI-infrastructure skepticism is partly reflected already: median AI-infra forward P/E fell from 32x to 22x, memory stocks are priced for roughly 50% earnings declines, and hyperscalers trade at their smallest P/E premium to the S&P 500 in a decade, so decelerating capex plus emerging monetization should support those shares.
